subject: Hosted API evaluation - quickstart, endpoints & rate limits
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme-retail.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API - quickstart & next steps (thanks for today!)

Hi Chris / Lina,

Thanks again for your time today — appreciated the thoughtful questions from the engineering team. Quick recap from our demo and the next steps to get you an evaluation of the Hosted API: 

- What we showed: Hosted API quickstart, streaming responses, example prompts for product recommendations, and the Redwood Console for per-route metrics.
- Quickstart resources attached: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf and a Postman collection (postman-sample-requests.json).
- Endpoints & auth: use POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate with your test API key (we'll provision you a scoped trial key tied to ACME-2026-324).
- Rate limits: default trial tier is 60 requests/min and 8 concurrent streams; see hosted-api-rate-limits.csv for details and burst behavior.
- Data handling: Hosted API does not persist your private prompts to train models; logs can be disabled — happy to share our data handling note if needed.

Questions we had on the call: you mentioned potential interest in Dedicated capacity if throughput or isolation needs exceed the Hosted limits — happy to scope numbers, but for the initial eval the Hosted API should be the fastest path.

Proposed next steps:
1) I'll provision a trial API key scoped to ACME and share credentials (target: today).
2) Aditya (SE) will join to help validate the Postman flows and walk through rate-limit behavior against your expected QPS.
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review performance and any Dedicated/Private fit-gap analysis.

If that works, can you confirm the engineer who should receive the API key (Lina?) and a preferred timeslot next week?

Attachments: redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB), hosted-api-rate-limits.csv (CSV), postman-sample-requests.json (JSON collection)

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0199
From: Chris Nolan <chris@acme-retail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acme-retail.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API - quickstart & next steps (thanks for today!)

Thanks Marissa — this is great. Lina is the engineer who will own the trial; please send the key to her. A couple of quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Can the trial API key be scoped to only allow requests from our IP range? We need to limit exposure while we test.
2) For rate limits: our expected steady-state is ~250 requests/min across multiple services with spikes up to ~900 for short periods during campaigns. If the Hosted trial is limited to 60 req/min, that sounds like it will be constraining. Can you advise if burst capacity or temporary higher limits are possible for the eval?

Also, security/compliance: we'll need a short note about data retention and whether logs can be turned off for specific keys. If Dedicated is a better fit long-term, please include a rough sizing and cost ballpark so we can include it in the procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Chris Nolan
Head of Engineering | Acme Retail
chris@acme-retail.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris@acme-retail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API - quickstart & next steps (thanks for today!)

Hi Chris — Aditya here (SE). Quick answers to your questions: 

1) IP restriction: yes, we can scope trial keys to an IP allowlist for Hosted API. Send over the CIDR ranges and we'll lock the key to those.

2) Rate limits / spikes: the default trial tier is conservative (60 req/min) to protect shared capacity. For evaluation purposes we can temporarily raise your rate limit to 300 req/min and increase concurrency to 20 streams for a 48–72 hour validation window. For sustained throughput at 250 steady and 900 peak we generally recommend Dedicated capacity — that gives you reserved GPU pools and guaranteed throughput with predictable latency.

Ballpark sizing for Dedicated given the numbers you shared: 2x A40-equivalent nodes with autoscale headroom (estimate) — I'll run a quick capacity model and share an initial monthly commit range and expected unit costs.

3) Data retention/logs: Hosted keys can be configured to disable request logging for specific keys. We also have Private (VPC/on-prem) for customers requiring full control and no outbound logs. I'll attach a short note on data handling and SOC2 evidence links.

Proposed immediate action: Marissa — if you can provision the IP-scoped trial key for Lina, I'll schedule a 60-minute session tomorrow to run concurrent tests and verify latency at the higher temporary limits. I'll bring a simple load script and sample prompts tailored to product-recs use case.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
Attachments: redwood-data-handling-summary.pdf (PDF, 0.6MB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Hi Lina — per Chris and Aditya, I've provisioned a scoped trial API key for ACME that is IP-locked to the CIDR ranges you provided (attached in HubSpot note). Key details below (separate secure email with the key itself sent):

- Trial window: 2026-09-01 10:00 PDT — 2026-09-04 10:00 PDT (48 hours at raised limits)
- Temporary limits: 300 req/min, 20 concurrent streams (burst tolerant for short windows)
- Logs: request logging disabled for this key per your request; see attached data handling note for confirmation.

Next: Aditya will run the load test tomorrow at 10:00 AM PT — can you confirm Lina that works? I've scheduled a 30-minute follow-up for Wed 2026-09-02 11:00 AM PT to review results and discuss Dedicated sizing if needed.
